description: God's discipline is not punishment. It leads to life and health. But we still resist it, and it costs us.
excerpt: We know it in our heads and we resist it with our lives. When conviction shows up, we do not want to hear it. When God is trying to redirect us, we drag our feet.
verse: "Lord, your discipline is good, for it leads to life and health. You restore my health and allow me to live!"
body_html:
This is the posture we should have.

We know it. Most of us who have walked with God for any length of time have heard it. His discipline is not punishment. It is not Him being harsh. It is not Him trying to make us miserable. His discipline is good. It leads to life and health. That is the whole point of it.

But we still push against it.

We know it in our heads and we resist it with our lives. When conviction shows up, we do not want to hear it. When God is trying to redirect us, we drag our feet. When He is asking us to lay something down, we grip it tighter. When He is disciplining us for our good, we act like He is the enemy.

And it costs us. Because when we refuse His discipline, we stay stuck way longer than we should. The thing He was trying to move us out of, we choose to stay in. The healing He was trying to bring, we delay. The life He wanted for us, we push off because we would not receive the correction that would get us there.

Hezekiah gets it here. He recognizes that what God did in his life, even the hard parts, was for his good. His discipline led to life. His discipline restored his health. His discipline was not something to run from. It was something to receive.

God is not disciplining us because He wants to hurt us. He is disciplining us because He loves us and wants more for us than the version of life we would settle for on our own. He has good plans. And sometimes the road to those good plans includes correction along the way.

I want to be someone who receives His discipline instead of resenting it. Someone who lets Him redirect me quickly instead of dragging out the process. Someone who sees His correction as a kindness.

Where has God been trying to discipline you, and are you receiving it or resisting it?
question: Where has God been trying to discipline you, and are you receiving it or resisting it?
